Visit note | 2025-12-31 11:00 AM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Jewel Gazi, 69, male. Mr. Gazi attends for his first visit, reporting that his eyelids have been stuck together in the morning and his left eye is very red. He is a shopkeeper, and he mentioned these symptoms started during an outbreak at an office in Dhanmondi. He denies any recent trauma, blurring of vision other than mild discharge, or sensitivity to light. Examination shows visual acuity 6/9 in the left eye, with a hyperaemic conjunctiva and mucopurulent discharge. Other vitals: BP 119/82 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 77 kg. Assessment: Bacterial conjunctivitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to wash his hands often, avoid sharing towels, and stay away from work for two days. Follow-up in 1 week if not better.

Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep her bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.
